evidence.detail: FR-PROXY-015 Requirement (docs/spec/22.reverse-proxy.srs.md, FR-PROXY-015 #### Requirement): "when writing the request body fails, it tries to read the response left on the socket, relays it when a complete status line and header block arrive, reports `INVALID_RESPONSE` otherwise" and "`CONNECT_FAILED` when the connection cannot be established". FR-PROXY-017 AC-5: "sending a 64 MiB body to a backend that never reads the request body gives 504 with `kind()` `WRITE_TIMEOUT` about 1 second after the socket buffers fill"; FR-PROXY-017 Requirement: "whichever is reached first applies, and the proxy reports `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `WRITE_TIMEOUT`, `READ_TIMEOUT` or `TOTAL_TIMEOUT` as 504 before the response". The write timeout and total timeout are enforced by closing the socket (REL-PROXY-002), so the body write fails and no response can be read from the closed socket: FR-PROXY-015's sentence yields INVALID_RESPONSE (and CONNECT_FAILED for a total timeout during the TCP connect), FR-PROXY-017 yields WRITE_TIMEOUT / TOTAL_TIMEOUT. The request scopes the early-response rule to a backend that closed the connection (§3.4: "백엔드가 본문을 다 읽기 전에 응답(401·413 등)을 보내고 연결을 닫아 쓰기가 실패하면 ... 읽지 못하면 `INVALID_RESPONSE`"; RST: "응답을 잃을 수 있습니다"), while the §3.4 table gives 쓰기 타임아웃 -> 504 `WRITE_TIMEOUT`. Only Implementation Notes (FR-PROXY-017: "the watchdog records which deadline fired so the failing call maps to `WRITE_TIMEOUT` or `TOTAL_TIMEOUT`") reconcile them; no requirement sentence or criterion does.

findings.description: A body-write failure caused by the write-timeout or total-timeout watchdog closing the socket falls under FR-PROXY-015's early-response rule (INVALID_RESPONSE) and under FR-PROXY-017 (WRITE_TIMEOUT/TOTAL_TIMEOUT) at once. A backend close or reset (no deadline fired) correctly gives INVALID_RESPONSE; a watchdog close must give the recorded deadline kind.

evidence.detail: SEC-PROXY-005 AC-5: "With `.connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS).totalTimeout(1, TimeUnit.SECONDS)`, a backend that accepts the TCP connection and never answers the TLS handshake gives 504 with `kind()` `TOTAL_TIMEOUT` after about 1 second". SEC-PROXY-005 Implementation Notes: "A handshake `SocketTimeoutException` is `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`; every other `SSLException` or `IOException` during the handshake or host name verification is `CONNECT_FAILED`, which the retry rules never retry." SEC-PROXY-005 Requirement: "report every TLS handshake or verification failure other than a handshake timeout as `CONNECT_FAILED`". The watchdog ends a handshake by closing the plain socket (REL-PROXY-002 Requirement), which surfaces as a SocketException (an IOException, not a SocketTimeoutException), so the notes and the requirement sentence classify it CONNECT_FAILED while AC-5 requires TOTAL_TIMEOUT.

findings.description: The kind mapping for a total-timeout watchdog close during the TLS handshake contradicts AC-5 of the same requirement.

evidence.detail: Request §3.9 (docs/naruserve-proxy-request.md, 응답 읽기): "본문 길이를 RFC 9112 §6.3의 순서대로 아래 표에 따라 정합니다", table rows in order: "HEAD 요청에 대한 응답, 204, 304 | 본문을 읽지 않음" before "`Transfer-Encoding`과 `Content-Length`가 함께 있음 | `INVALID_RESPONSE`" and "`Content-Length`가 숫자만으로 이루어지지 않음 ... | `INVALID_RESPONSE`"; the separate malformed list ("표와 별개로") does not include these two. PRD-155: "이 응답들은 길이 헤더와 관계없이 본문 없이 끝난 것으로 본다." FR-PROXY-014 AC-6: "A response to a HEAD request, a 204 and a 304 whose header block carries both `Content-Length` and `Transfer-Encoding`, or `Content-Length: abc`, each give 502 with `kind()` `INVALID_RESPONSE`, because the framing headers are checked before the body is skipped."
